clean: Hi Ruth, I'm writing from the hospital cafeteria because the internet in Dad's room is terrible. The surgery went well. The doctor came out at about 2 and said everything looked clean and he should be walking by tomorrow afternoon, which I find hard to believe, but okay. that is groggy and keeps asking if the dog has been fed. I told them five times that she has. Mom is a wreck but she's pretending she isn't, so I'm making her eat something every couple of hours. The nurse says visiting hours ended at 8, so I'll be here till then, and if you want to call, the best time is probably around 7, when he's had dinner and he's in the sleep. I'll put you on speaker. Don't bring up the golf trip, he's still sore about it. I'll write again tomorrow.

Probably caught the bittest fish of my life this morning. You should have been there. We went out to the lake at 4:30 because Zomar insisted that's when they bite, and for three hours nothing. I was freezing and bored and about to quit, and then my line goes tight and I nearly dropped a rod. It takes me 20 minutes to reel it in, and it's a pike, easily three feet long, I'm not exaggerating. Omar has the photo outside there. We let it go obviously, but my arms are still shaking. The best part is the guy on the next boat was watching the whole time and he gave me a thumbs up, so now I'm famous at the marina. We're going again next Saturday if you want to come.

Dear Sophia, I've been putting off this email because I didn't quite know how to say it. I lost my job in March. They laid off about 40 people, and I was one of them, which was a shock, because I'd just been promoted. The first month I was kind of a mess. I slept till noon and watched terrible television. Then I made myself a schedule, get up, go for a walk, apply to three jobs a day, and slowly it started to feel less awful. I had four interviews in May and I started a new company on the 1st of July, so the story has a happy ending. I just didn't want you to hear it from someone else. Thank you for the card you sent. It was exactly what I needed. I'd love to catch up properly. Are you free for a call this Sunday? Let me know. Much love Breedy

My neighbor, you know the guy with the leaf blower, he comes over at 7 in the morning on a Sunday, a Sunday, and says he's been getting complaints about my garbage cans, and I'm like, from who, and he says the whole street, and I look at the street, and there's nobody to call the sack with four houses, and two of them are empty, so I say, okay, what exactly is wrong with the cans, and he says they're visible from the road, which is where cans fill, that's the point of a road. Anyway, I said I'd think about it, and then I went inside and had a very large coffee, and I think I'm going to buy a really ugly gnome and put it next to the cans just to see what he says.

Marcus, congratulations, I mean it. I read your message three times and I'm still grinning. Girl and 8 pounds 2 ounces, that's a proper size. How's Rebecca doing? I hope she's getting some sleep. I know she will be. I remember when our born, we didn't sleep for a month and I put the car keys in the fridge twice. Anyway, we want to bring over some food, lasagna, soup, whatever you'd like. Just tell us what you need and what you don't, and we promise not to stay long. I know the first week is a lot. If you'd rather have no visitors that's totally fine, just say the word. Give her a kiss from us, and a very small hat. I knitted one PLO. It's terrible, I'm sorry in advance. With all our love, Nina and Andre

The power went out at about 4 yesterday and I was alone with the kids, which was a nightmare. I was prepared though. We have candles, and a camping stove, and a whole box of board games, so we made a fort in the living room, and we had soup on the stove, and played Monopoly by flashlight. At some point my daughter said, this is the best day ever, and I thought, wow, all it took was a blackout. The power came back at 9 and everyone groaned, which I did not expect. We turned it off again for another hour, just because. My husband got home at 10 and said, what's going on, because the whole house was dark and we were all in a fort. I said, you missed it, and he did.

Alright, for the camping trip I need you to pick up three things:
1. The tent from my garage, the green one, not the blue one.
2. A bag of charcoal, the big bag.
3. The cooler from your dad's place.
I know it's a pain, I'll owe you. We're leaving at 6 on Friday, so please have everything in your car by Thursday night. I'll bring the food, and Zara is bringing the little speaker, not the huge one. We don't want to annoy the other campers. The site is by the river, so it'll be cold that night. Pack a real jacket, not a hoodie. Thanks, you're a legend.

Hello darling, it's Grandma. I am calling because I tried to use the new tablet you gave me and I press something in. Now everything is very big. The letters are enormous. I can only see three words on the screen. I called your uncle and he said to go to settings, but I cannot find the settings. There is a little picture of a gear, is that it? I pressed it and it made a noise. Now the screen has gone black. I think I have broken it. Please don't be angry. I am going to put it in the drawer and wait for you to come on Sunday. Bring the cable, and some of that nice cheese you bought last time, the one with the blue. I will make tea. Goodbye darling, kiss kiss.

Hi, it's me. I just got out of the school open house and I have thoughts. Jonas's teacher says he's doing great in math, which surprised me, because he told me he hates it, but apparently he finished the whole workbook two weeks early, and she's moving him up a group. In reading he's fine, but she said he talks too much, which, yes, I know, where do you think he gets it? And then she said he's been drawing in the margins of his tests, and she showed me one, and it's a really detailed drawing of a dragon eating a school bus. I wanted to be mad but it was actually pretty good. Anyway, I told her we talked to him. I think we should just buy him a sketchbook. I'll be home by 8, don't let him stay up.

Hi Andre, you mentioned your broker was good and I wanted to ask for details. We've been renting for eight years and finally think we can buy. We've saved about $40,000, which doesn't sound like much but it's taken us forever, and our credit scores are fine, I think. Mine is 740 and my wife's is 710. The problem is I'm self-employed, so the banks keep asking for two years of statements, and I only have 19 months, because I started in February of the year before last. So I was hoping someone who knows the system could tell us whether it's worth trying now or whether we should wait. I don't want to waste your time. I'll pay for a consultation if that's how it works. Let me know, thanks a lot, Amara

Dear Mrs. Patterson, I wanted to apologize in writing for the noise on Saturday night. We had a few people over for my daughter's 21st and I'm afraid the music went on much later than we agreed. I know you said 11, and it was closer to midnight. That's entirely our fault. I've spoken to everyone involved, and it won't happen again. I would also like to offer to replace your flowerpot, which I'm told was knocked over by a guest. I have no idea who, but I found the pieces in the morning. Please let me know the cost, and I'd be glad to bring over a pie as well. My apple pie is quite good, if I say so myself. Again, I am truly sorry. Yours sincerely, Helen

I need to tell you about the worst haircut of my life. I went to this new place, because my usual guy retired, and I said just a trim. I even showed her a photo, and she nodded and smiled, and then she started cutting and I realised she was cutting a lot, a lot, and I'm sitting there frozen, because what are you supposed to say? And by the time she finished I had a bowl cut. I'm 34 years old, I look like a mushroom. I paid, I tipped, I said thank you. I'm a coward. And now I'm wearing a hat. I'm going to wear a hat until it grows back, which is going to be a while, so if you see me at work and I'm in a hat, don't ask, just nod.

Okay, house meeting thoughts. The kitchen is a crime scene. There's a pot in the sink that has been there since Monday, and I know it's not mine because I don't own a pot that color. I'm not angry, I'm just disappointed. Can we agree on a rota? I'll take the bins and the bathroom, Nadia can do the floors, and whoever cooks doesn't wash up, the others do. I'm making a chart and sticking it on the fruit, don't fight me on it. Also, somebody keeps eating my yogurt. I've labeled it, twice. I'm not naming names, but his name is Sam.

I manage a bank branch and I need to draft an announcement to my staff about the new queue system. The background is that we've had complaints about wait times on Friday afternoons, sometimes, and corporate is rolling out numbered tickets starting the 1st of next month. I don't want it to sound like a punishment. Keep it warm but direct, under 200 words, and mention the training is on the 22nd at 9 Please write it as an email from me. My name is Bill and don't add a subject line.

I'm the sales obsolete at a mid size SaaS company and I want you to help me analyze why our win rate dropped. Here's what I know, it went from 31% to 24% over two quarters, the biggest drop is in deals over $50,000, and we hired five new reps in that window. I don't have the data in front of me, so don't make up numbers. Just give me a list of hypotheses to check, ranked by how likely they are, and for each one tell me which report in a CRM I'd pull to test it.

Hi Marcus, thanks for waiting on the oak dining table. Quick update, the boards arrived on Tuesday but three of them had a bad warp, so I sent them back and the replacements won't be here until the 18th. That pushes your delivery from the 25th to about the 2nd of November. I know that's later than we promised and I'm sorry about it. To make up for it, I'll include the matching bench at no charge, and I can bring everything over myself instead of using the free company. Let me know if the new date works and I'll lock it in. Thanks, Hecker

I want you to act as a skeptical loan officer. I'm going to paste in a small business loan application next and I want you to read it the way a tough underwriter would. Look for gaps in cash flow, anything that doesn't add up between the tax returns and the projections, and any red flags in the debt to income ratio. Don't be polite about it. After that, rewrite the weakest section so it's stronger but keep it honest, and tell me what supporting documents I should attach. Start by asking me anything you need to know about the business.

I call on a bookstore and we're writing the copy for our new loyalty program. The idea is simple, you get a stamp for every $10 you spend and 10 stamps gets you a free paperback up to $18. Our voice is friendly and a little nerdy but never salesy. I need three versions of the announcement for our newsletter, one short, one medium, one long, and each one should end with a question for the readers. Do not use exclamation points, we have a rule about that, and please don't call the members bookworms, we've been over there.

I need to prep for a performance review conversation with one of my tellers at the bank branch. She's been there three years, great with customers, but a cash drawer has been off by small amounts four times this quarter. I want to be fair, I don't want her to feel attacked. Can you give me an opening statement, a list of questions I should ask, and a way to bring up the drawer issue without making it sound like an accusation? Keep the tone supportive and ask me what I already know about her situation before you start.

I have a layover in Istanbul for 9 hours on the 12th of March and I've never been. I land at 7:40 in the morning, my next flight is at 4:15, and I'll have one carry on bag. I don't speak Turkish. Can you plan how I spend those hours, including how to get from the airport into the old city, what to see if I only have maybe 4 hours of actual sightseeing, or to eat something local without getting ripped off, and when I should head back to make sure I'm for security with plenty of time?

My team is kind of drowning in follow up emails and I want to build a prompt template we can all reuse. The template should take a prospect's name, their company, and what we talked about last, and then write a follow up that's under 120 words. It should sound like a person wrote it, not like a robot, so no phrases like I hope this email finds you well. Include one clear next step and a linked placeholder for booking time. Can you write the template and then show me an example using a fake prospect named Dana at some company called Bright Path?

I'm writing an email to my cooking class students about the canceled session and I want you to draft it. The reason is the instructor, that's me, broke my wrist on Sunday, so I can't hold a knife for about three weeks. I feel terrible about it, I mean it. Offer them either a refund or a credit toward the next series, and tell them the decision is due by the end of the month. Warm tone, short paragraphs, and don't make it sound like a legal notice. Sign it Dominic.

We're redesigning the lobby at our bank branch and I want to brainstorm with you. The lobby is about 30 feet by 40, there's one door, two ATMs along the east wall, and four teller windows. The problem is that the line for the ATMs blocks the entrance. I need five layout ideas that fix that without moving the teller windows because the plumbing and security glass are fixed to scrat each idea in two or three sentences, say what it costs roughly, low, medium, or high, and tell me which one you pick and why.
